source_refs.note: v. Redox Potential: a main subheading of 33.1 Properties and Quality of Water, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 247-249.

blocks.text: The redox potential of water is a measure of the oxidising and reducing nature of a water body. In well-oxygenated water, chemical species exist in their most oxidised forms, such as SO₄²⁻ and CO₂. However, in polluted or stagnant water, where oxygen is depleted, the environment becomes reducing. This leads to the formation of toxic substances like hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) and ammonia (NH₃). Understanding these chemical equilibria and the molecular behaviour of H₂O allows us to predict how specific contaminants will migrate, transform, and ultimately impact the global water supply.

blocks.prompt: i. Explain how the polarity of water facilitates the transport of agricultural pollutants like pesticides into the water cycle.
blocks.explanation: Water is polar, so it dissolves polar organic compounds and ions. Polar pesticides and herbicides dissolve in rain and runoff and are carried to rivers, lakes and groundwater, where they persist.

blocks.prompt: ii. Differentiate between Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) and Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) as indicators of water quality.
blocks.explanation: BOD is the oxygen used by microorganisms to break down organic matter (over five days at 20 °C); it measures only biodegradable organic pollution. COD is the oxygen needed to oxidise both organic and inorganic substances chemically with oxidising agents such as KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇; it measures the total pollution load. COD is therefore usually higher than BOD. (The book prints 'Biological' here; the text above says 'Biochemical' Oxygen Demand.)
